Semi-supervised learning has been a popular approach for training deep neural networks, but its effectiveness is often hindered by the quality of pseudo labels generated by the model. To address this issue, we introduce FlexMatch, a novel method that leverages a curriculum learning strategy to dynamically adjust the quality of pseudo labels. By incorporating a confidence threshold, FlexMatch selectively uses high-quality pseudo labels to train the model, while discarding low-quality ones. Our approach is flexible and can be easily integrated with existing semi-supervised learning methods, leading to improved performance on various benchmark datasets. Notably, FlexMatch achieves state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-1K, with significant gains of 0.4%, 0.6%, and 0.5% in top-1 accuracy, respectively.
